headline: Approved 20 items, including a $30,000,000 school bus renewal and a $10,500,000 special education bus renewal.
summary: The committee approved 20 items, mostly contracts, renewals, and amendments. Two members voted no on the $30,000,000 school bus renewal, which still passed 5-2. The committee also heard a second grade literacy update and set an October 22, 2026 town hall date.
decisions: Approved 7-0 the request that Shia Anyce Carelock be awarded a City of Springfield Diploma.
Approved 7-0 Central High School's Girls Basketball overnight field trip to the Nike Tournament of Champions in Phoenix, AZ, December 17 to December 23, 2026.
Approved 5-2 Renewal Option No. 2 to City Contract No. 20250008 for school bus transportation services, $30,000,000.00. Valentin and Monroe Naylor voted no.
Approved 7-0 Renewal Option No. 2 to City Contract No. 20250523 for student transportation services and bus pass system, $800,000.00.
Approved 7-0 City Contract No. 20270020 for out-of-district tuition and special education services, $4,500,000.00.
Approved 7-0 Amendment No. 1 to City Contract No. 20230851 for professional development services, $1,152,874.00.
Approved 7-0 Amendment No. 1 to City Contract No. 20250023 for educational materials and professional development, $2,000,000.00.
Approved 7-0 City Contract No. 20270032 for out-of-district tuition for special education students, $1,500,000.00.
Approved 7-0 Amendment No. 4 and Notice of Exercise of Renewal Option No. 4 to City Contract No. 20230148 for out-of-district tuition and special education services, $3,000,000.00.
Approved 7-0 City Contract No. 20270042 for the Rising First Grader Daily Reading Program, $2,232,500.00.
Approved 7-0 Notice of Exercise of Renewal Option No. 1 to City Contract No. 20260497 with Holyoke Community College for the Gateway to College Program, $272,000.00.
Approved 7-0 City Contract No. 20270015 for sole source science curriculum materials, digital licenses, and professional development, $2,608,715.60.
Approved 7-0 Amendment No. 3 and Renewal No. 2 to City Contract No. 20240923A for educational material and professional development services, $300,000.00.
Approved 7-0 Renewal Option No. 2 to City Contract No. 20250021 for nursing services, $300,000.00.
Approved 7-0 Renewal Option No. 2 to City Contract No. 20250095 for school bus transportation for McKinney Vento students, $3,000,000.00.
Approved 7-0 Renewal Option No. 2 to City Contract No. 20250088 for school bus transportation for special education in/OOD, $10,500,000.00.
Approved 7-0 City Contract No. 20270089 for lease of copiers and printers, $2,155,006.08.
Approved 7-0 the assignment and first amendment to City Contract No. 20240600 with American International College.
Approved 7-0 City Contract No. 20270012 with Xerox Business Solutions, LLC for copy center operations and mail courier services, $3,337,221.60.
Approved 7-0 Notice of Renewal Option No. 4 for City Contract No. 20230453 for alternative school transportation for special needs students, $600,000.00.
Agreed to proceed with the October 22, 2026 town hall date.
Continued the selection of a School Committee representative for the Influence 100 Fellowship to the October 10th meeting, after the October 8th orientation.

decision_evidence.quote: Motion passes to approve the request to the School Committee that Shia Anyce Carelock be awarded a City of Springfield Diploma.

Motion passes to approve Central High School’s Girls Basketball overnight field trip request to the Nike Tournament of Champions in Phoenix, AZ leaving on December 17, 2026, and returning December 23, 2026.

Motion passes to approve Renewal Option No. 2 to City Contract No. 20250008 Agreement for School Bus Transportation Services for 72 Passengers Buses, 83 Passenger Busses, and Type A Minibuses for the Springfield Public Schools in the amount of $30,000,000.00.

Motion passes to approve Renewal Option No. 2 to City Contract No. 20250523 Agreement for Student Transportation Services on Public Mass Transit and Student Bus Pass System for Springfield Public Schools 2024-2027 in the amount of $800,000.00.

Motion passes to approve City Contract No. 20270020 Agreement for Out of District Tuition for Special Education Students as required by 603 CMR 28.06(3) and Special Education Services for the Springfield Public Schools in the amount of $4,500,000.00.
Motion passes to approve Amendment No. 1 to City Contract No. 20230851 Agreement for Professional Development Services for Springfield Public Schools in the amount of $1,152,874.00.

Motion passes to approve Amendment No. 1 to City Contract No. 20250023 Agreement for the Purchase of Educational Materials and Professional Development Services for the Springfield School Department in the amount of $2,000,000.00.
Motion passes to approve City Contract No. 20270032 Agreement for Out of District Tuition for Special Education Students as required by 603 CMR 28.06(3) in the amount of $1,500,000.00.

Motion passes to approve Amendment No. 4 and Notice of Exercise of Renewal Option No. 4 to City Contract No. 20230148 Agreement for Out of District Tuition and Special Education Services for the School Department in the amount of $3,000,000.00.
Motion passes to approve City Contract No. 20270042 Agreement for the Rising First Grader Daily Reading Program for the Springfield Public Schools in the amount of $2,232,500.00.

Motion passes to approve the Notice of Exercise of Renewal Option No. 1 to City Contract No. 20260497 Memorandum of Understanding Gateway to College Program at Holyoke Community College in the amount of $272,000.00.

Motion passes to approve City Contract No. 20270015 Agreement for Sole Source Science Curriculum Materials, Digital Licenses and Professional Development for the Springfield Public School Department in the amount of $2,608,715.60.

Motion passes to approve Amendment No. 3 and Renewal No. 2 to City Contract No. 20240923A Agreement for Educational Material and Professional Development Services for Springfield Public Schools in the amount of $300,000.00.
Motion passes to approve Renewal Option No. 2 to City Contract No. 20250021 Agreement for Nursing Services for the Springfield Public Schools in the amount of $300,000.00.

Motion passes to approve Renewal Option No. 2 to City Contract No. 20250095 Agreement for School Bus Transportation Services for McKinney Vento Students for the Springfield Public Schools in the amount of $3,000,000.00.

Motion passes to approve Renewal Option No. 2 to City Contract No. 20250088 Agreement for School Bus Transportation Services for Special Education in/OOD for the Springfield Public Schools in the amount of $10,500,000.00.
Motion passes to approve City Contract No. 20270089 Agreement for Lease of Copiers/Printers for Springfield Public Schools in the amount of $2,155,006.08.
Motion passes to approve Assignment and First Amendment to City Contract No. 20240600 Agreement between American International College and the Springfield Public Schools.

Motion passes to approve City Contract No. 20270012 Agreement for Springfield Public Schools Copy Center Operations/Sales Services Mail Courier with Xerox Business Solutions, LLC in the amount of $3,337,221.60.

Motion passes to approve the Notice of Renewal Option No. 4 for City Contract No. 20230453 Agreement for Alternative School Transportation for Special Needs Students on an “As Needed” Basis in the amount of $600,000.00.
Following discussion, the School Committee agreed to proceed with the October 22, 2026 town hall date.

Members discussed scheduling considerations and agreed to revisit the matter after the Influence 100 orientation on October 8th, with the selection of the School Committee representative scheduled for consideration at the October 10th meeting.

IV. PRESENTATIONS: 
A. Second Grade Literacy. The School Committee received an update on the district’s early literacy 
priority, which aims for students to become proficient readers by the end of second grade. District 
literacy leaders emphasized that the goal builds upon Springfield’s investment in Universal Pre-K 
and reflects the importance of strong literacy skills as a foundation for future academic and 
postsecondary success. 
 
The presentation reviewed the science of reading, noting that effective literacy instruction extends 
beyond phonics and includes word recognition, handwriting, spelling, comprehension, and 
composition through structured, explicit, systematic, and data-driven instruction. Early literacy 
screening data showed encouraging progress during the 2025–2026 school year. Kindergarten 
students at or above benchmark increased from 30% at the beginning of the year to 60% at year-
end; first grade increased from 40% to 60%; and second grade increased from 44% to 54%. Year-
over-year comparisons also showed improvements across all three grade levels. Gains were also 
reported among exceptional learners and multilingual learners, although staff stressed that the data 
remains urgent and continued improvement is necessary. 
 
Staff outlined the district’s early literacy strategy beginning in Pre-K, including multiple 
assessments used to monitor developmental, literacy, writing, and kindergarten-readiness skills. 
The information is intended to create a literacy profile for students before they enter kindergarten 
and inform districtwide instructional planning. Professional development for Pre-K educators 
includes evidence-based literacy instruction, oral language development, emergent literacy, 
social-emotional skills, self-regulation, and inclusive instructional practices. Elementary educators 
and administrators are also receiving continued training on literacy screening, data-informed 
instruction, intervention strategies, and structured literacy. Additional work is occurring in 
collaboration with the Exceptional Learners and Multilingual Learners departments. 
 
The School Committee also received an update on high-dosage literacy tutoring through Ignite 
Reading. The district will have approximately 1,643 first- and second-grade tutoring seats, 
including 750 first-grade seats funded by DESE and 893 second-grade seats approved by the 
Committee. Students receive approximately 15 minutes of individualized tutoring each school day 
from trained Ignite Reading tutors. Staff reported that of the 849 first graders who began the 
program last year, approximately 90% started at least a year behind. By year-end, 72% had 
progressed into middle- or end-of-first-grade skills, 8% had advanced into early second-grade 
skills, and 9% had completed the program after demonstrating mastery of second-grade standards.

Staff noted, however, that approximately 1,900 students were identified as needing intervention, 
meaning available tutoring seats currently do not meet the full identified need. 
 
School Committee members asked how students with dyslexia or other reading disabilities are 
identified and supported. Staff clarified that the district’s literacy screener does not diagnose 
dyslexia but identifies students who may be at risk for reading difficulties. Structured literacy 
benefits students with dyslexia, while additional evaluation and intervention are coordinated with 
the Exceptional Learners Department. Continued attention to appropriate Tier 2 and Tier 3 
interventions was identified as important. 
 
Questions were also raised regarding the distribution of tutoring seats, student mobility, and 
access for newly enrolled students. Staff confirmed that tutoring is available across elementary 
schools and that efforts are made to have a tutoring seat follow a student who transfers between 
schools. If that cannot occur, the vacated seat may be reassigned. Students who progress 
sufficiently can also graduate from the program, allowing seats to be made available to other 
students. District-funded seats provide greater flexibility regarding grade level and student 
eligibility than the DESE-funded first-grade seats. 
 
The School Committee further discussed the Pre-K screening timeline, with staff confirming that 
the Early Screening Inventory must be administered within 45 days of a student’s enrollment. 
Members also asked about Ignite Reading tutors, language support, and when tutoring takes place. 
Staff explained that tutors are hired and extensively trained by Ignite Reading, may be matched 
with students who share their home language when possible, and provide tutoring during the 
regular school day. Staff highlighted the strong relationships students have developed with their 
tutors and noted positive effects on confidence and social-emotional well-being. 
 
Finally, members asked about increasing family engagement in literacy development. Staff 
reported that Ignite Reading and the district have family resources available and identified 
stronger home-school connections as a goal for the coming year, including the possibility of 
family literacy nights and informational sessions for families of participating students.

VII. REPORT OF THE SUPERINTENDENT: 
A. Superintendent Dr. Sonia Dinnall welcomed the School Committee back for the new school year 
and provided an overview of district accomplishments, student outcomes, and priorities for the 
2026–27 school year. She reported that the August 13th administrative meeting was well received 
following adjustments made in response to administrator feedback and noted that school leaders 
are prepared and supported to begin the year successfully. She also recognized the School 
Committee’s participation in Convocation and highlighted the importance of unity and 
collaboration across the district. 
 
The Superintendent highlighted several academic accomplishments, including schools and 
students achieving scores of 500 or higher on MCAS and MCAS-Alt assessments. She recognized 
schools that demonstrated significant improvements in student performance and emphasized that 
continued work is necessary to increase achievement across the district. She also reported 
significant decreases in chronic absenteeism at several schools and credited school leaders and the 
district attendance team for their efforts to improve student attendance. 
 
The School Committee was updated on FAFSA completion, noting a districtwide nine-
percentage-point increase and strong completion rates at several high schools. The Superintendent 
emphasized the importance of FAFSA completion in providing students access to college 
financial aid, career pathways, and Pell Grant funding, including opportunities related to technical 
education. She also reported an increase in advanced coursework completion from 46.4% in 2024 
to 50% in 2025 and an increase in MCAS completion from 53% in 2025 to 58% in 2026. A two-
percentage-point increase in immediate postsecondary enrollment was also noted. 
 
The Superintendent recognized the district’s Career and Technical Education accomplishments, 
including numerous industry-recognized certifications earned by graduating students in areas such 
as OSHA, CPR/First Aid, CNA, Microsoft, Google Digital Marketing, Adobe Photoshop, 
refrigeration, CompTIA, barbering, and early childhood education. She emphasized that these 
credentials provide students with additional opportunities for postsecondary education and 
employment. 
 
The Superintendent also recognized the accomplishments of Springfield Public Schools student-
athletes, including Western Massachusetts and state qualifiers, championship and runner-up 
teams, individual wrestling champions, swimming achievements, and baseball accomplishments. 
Visual and performing arts programs were also highlighted, including the district’s efforts to 
provide rigorous, enriching, and meaningful music and performing arts opportunities across all 71 
schools. The Superintendent recognized the leadership of the district’s visual and performing arts 
team and the contributions of Ignite mentors and SPS graduates who return to support current
